Droplets of rain ran down the window.
A single droplet fell from the leaky tap.

easy.def: A person who leaves school or a program before finishing.
examples: The dropout left school.
He was a dropout.
A dropout missed class.

more.def: A person who leaves school or a course before it is finished.
examples: The dropout later went back to school and graduated.
A few students became dropouts from the program.
Teachers try to help every student so no one becomes a dropout.

easy.def: A long time with no rain.
examples: The plants died in the drought.
The pond dried up in the drought.
There was no water to spare in the drought.

more.def: A long period with little or no rain, so the land becomes very dry.
examples: During the drought, the farmers' fields turned brown.
After the long drought, the river was only a trickle.
The town asked people to save water during the drought.

easy.def: To die because you are in water and cannot breathe.
examples: The lifeguard watches so no one will drown.
A tiny ant almost drowned in a puddle.
The sailors were saved before they could drown.

more.def: To die by breathing in water because you cannot get air.
examples: Lifeguards are trained to rescue swimmers who might drown.
The little mouse nearly drowned when it fell in the rain barrel.
The sailors wore life jackets, so they did not drown when the boat tipped.

easy.def: To be half asleep.
examples: The dog drowsed in the sun.
Grandpa drowsed in the chair.
I drowsed on the bus.

more.def: To be half asleep; to doze.
examples: The cat drowsed in the sun.
Grandpa drowsed in his chair.
I drowsed during the long ride.

easy.def: In a sleepy way.
examples: She yawned drowsily.
He blinked drowsily.
The baby smiled drowsily.

more.def: In a sleepy way, as if about to fall asleep.
examples: She yawned drowsily and rubbed her eyes.
The cat blinked drowsily at the fire.
He nodded drowsily in the warm car.

easy.def: Sleepy.
examples: I am drowsy.
The drowsy cat yawned.
The drowsy child nodded.

more.def: Feeling sleepy and ready to go to sleep.
examples: I felt drowsy after the long walk.
The drowsy cat curled up on the couch.
A warm bath made the child drowsy.

easy.def: Medicine that helps you get well.
examples: The doctor gave me a drug for my cough.
This drug helps with pain.
A grown-up must give you a drug.

more.def: A medicine used to treat an illness or pain.
examples: The doctor prescribed a drug to fight the infection.
Scientists are testing a new drug for allergies.
Some drugs come as pills and others as liquids.

easy.def: A shop that sells medicine and other things you need.
examples: We went to the drugstore.
Mom bought a bandage at the drugstore.
The drugstore is open.

more.def: A store that sells medicine, bandages and other everyday things.
examples: Mom bought cough medicine at the drugstore.
The drugstore on the corner also sells cards and candy.
He walked to the drugstore to pick up a bandage and soap.

easy.def: A round musical instrument that you hit.
examples: I play the drum.
The drum is loud.
She hit the drum.

more.def: A hollow instrument that you hit with sticks or your hands to make a beat.
examples: The drum beat fast during the parade.
He plays the drums in the band.
She tapped the drum with two sticks.

easy.def: The sound of a drum.
examples: We heard a drumbeat.
The drumbeat was loud.
A steady drumbeat.

more.def: The sound or rhythm made by beating a drum.
examples: We heard the steady drumbeat of the parade.
The drumbeat grew louder as the band came near.
Her heart kept time with the drumbeat.

easy.def: A person who plays the drums.
examples: The drummer kept the beat.
My brother is a drummer.
The drummer played loud.

more.def: A person who plays the drums.
examples: The drummer kept the beat while the band played.
My brother is a drummer in the school band.
The drummer struck the cymbals at the end of the song.

easy.def: A long, fast drum beat before an announcement.
examples: There was a drumroll.
A drumroll is a fast beat.
The drumroll began.

more.def: A fast, continuous beating of a drum, often to build excitement.
examples: The drummer played a drumroll.
There was a drumroll before the winner was named.
A drumroll builds excitement.

easy.def: A stick for playing a drum, or a chicken leg.
examples: The drummer holds a drumstick.
I ate a drumstick.
The drumstick is wood.

more.def: A stick used to hit a drum, or the lower part of a cooked chicken or turkey leg.
examples: The drummer twirled his drumstick.
I ate a chicken drumstick for dinner.
Her drumstick tapped the drum.

easy.def: Not wet.
examples: The towel is dry.
My hair is dry.
The ground is dry.

more.def: Not wet, with no water on it.
examples: The towel was dry by the afternoon.
The dry ground was cracked.
Desert plants live where it is dry.

easy.def: To take away water.
examples: Dry your hands.
The sun dries the clothes.
I dried the dishes.

more.def: To take water away from something, or to lose its water.
examples: Dry your hands on the towel.
The sun dried the laundry on the line.
I dried the dishes after dinner.

easy.def: A machine that dries clothes.
examples: I put my wet socks in the dryer.
The dryer is warm.
Dad turned on the dryer.

more.def: A machine that uses warm air to dry things, such as clothes or hair.
examples: Mom took the warm towels out of the dryer.
A hair dryer blows hot air to dry wet hair.
The dryer buzzed when the clothes were done.

easy.def: In a calm, funny way that does not show a smile.
examples: "Nice weather," he said dryly.
She dryly said, "How lovely."
He joked dryly.

more.def: In a calm, quiet way that is funny but does not show it.
examples: "That went well," he said dryly as the cake collapsed.
She dryly remarked that the bus was only an hour late.
He dryly joked about the rain.
